sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin**: Founded by **Bhagat Jawahar Mal** (Sian Sahib) in 1840 in Western Punjab.
• **Ideological Shift**: Transformed from a puritanical reform movement (Namdhari) to a political rebellion under **Ram Singh**.
• **Core Tenets**: Advocacy of **Swadeshi**, boycott of British education/courts, and promotion of **Khadi**.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The movement was the first to use **Non-Cooperation** as a political weapon against the British Raj.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Focus on purity, anti-caste, and widow remarriage; Western Punjab.
Reaction to moral decay and loss of Sikh identity post-annexation.
Focus on Swadeshi, boycott, and anti-cow slaughter; Central Punjab.
Reaction to British administrative oppression and cultural encroachment.

items.definition: Followers who believe in the 'Name' (Naam) of God; they wear white clothes and carry a wooden stick (lathi).
Administrative divisions created by Ram Singh to organize the movement across Punjab, showing a parallel government structure.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Swadeshi & Boycott**: Established their own postal system and judicial panchayats to bypass British institutions.
• **Anti-Cow Slaughter**: A central pillar of their religious identity that led to direct violent clashes with British-backed butchers.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Brutal suppression by British (1872 Malerkotla incident) and exile of Ram Singh to Rangoon.
• **Solutions**: The movement's legacy of non-cooperation was later institutionalized by the Indian National Congress.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'K-S-R-N' (Kuka, Swadeshi, Ram Singh, Non-cooperation).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Kuka movement led by Ram Singh focused on Swadeshi and pioneered Non-cooperation.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not confuse Kuka Movement with the Akali Movement. Kuka (1840s-70s) was a 19th-century precursor; Akali (1920s) was a 20th-century movement for Gurdwara reform.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Proto-Nationalist' to describe the Kuka movement, highlighting how it linked local religious grievances to broader anti-imperialist sentiment.

keyTakeaways: The Kuka movement was the first organized movement in Punjab to use non-cooperation as a political tool.
Ram Singh's exile to Rangoon in 1872 effectively ended the militant phase of the movement.
The movement is historically significant for its early emphasis on Swadeshi and boycott of British institutions.
